children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Friday.
WHEAT - Down 3 to 5 cents per bushel
ease on technical selling and profit taking ahead of the weekend. Declines kept in check by ongoing concerns about tighter global supplies as the Russia-Ukraine war restricts Black Sea grain exports.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was last down 4 cents at $7.23 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was down 2-1/2 cents at $7.92 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last down 1-1/2 cents at $7.51 a bushel.
CORN - Steady to down 2 cents per bushel

futures flat to weaker as crude oil prices eased and as traders squared positions ahead of the weekend. Tighter supplies, with war restricting Black Sea exports and smaller-than-anticipated crops in key world growing areas, underpinned prices.
The International Grains Council said on Thursday it had trimmed its forecast for 2026/27 global corn production with crop outlooks reduced for the United States, the European Union and India.

French maize crop conditions worsened last week to hit another record low, data from farm office FranceAgriMer showed on Friday, as hot, dry weather persisted in the European Union's biggest grain producer.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last down 1 cent at $5.29-1/2 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Down 8 to 12 cents per bushel

ease on technical selling and profit taking ahead of the weekend, and as soymeal futures retreated from the week's highs. Expectations for Chinese buying ahead of a summit between presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump next week underpinned the market.
Traders will be watching for any news from a weekend meeting between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng which will set the stage for the Trump-Xi summit.
The US Department of Agriculture on Friday reported private sales of 111,000 metric tons of US soybeans to China.
China's state stockpiler, Sinograin, has resumed large-scale auctions of imported soybeans after a pause of roughly a month.

Brazil's 2026 soybean exports are expected to total 115 million metric tons, crushers group Abiove said on Friday, lowering its forecast by 400,000 tons after top importer China stepped up purchases of US soybeans.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last down 11 cents at $13.08-3/4 per bushel.
